title: One Sandbox, two Workspaces
blurb: Separate overlays in one Sandbox, a slow build left to a background job, an fs write that makes a mount stale, and the refusals that keep teardown explicit: MountsActive, Busy, Dirty.

root.say: Two Branches in one Sandbox: docs and site each get a Workspace.

bash.description: Fork docs and site; mount both in one Sandbox

root.note: docs is /workspaces/1 and site is /workspaces/2 in the same Sandbox. The overlays are separate: site cannot see docs/guide.md.

root.say: The site build is slow. I'll leave it to a background job and keep working.
Meanwhile: a quick changelog on docs without the shell, and what teardown refuses while things are in flight.

bash.description: Write on docs; try to close and unmount

root.note: The fs write is allowed while docs is mounted, and leaves that Workspace stale. close never unmounts implicitly; a running build still owns site's mount.

root.say: Now I wait for the build.
The build is done. Committing docs, then unmounting both.
root.note: Commit merges the stale docs Workspace with the head, keeping CHANGELOG.md and the guide. Unmount never drops work silently: site's build output needs an explicit discard.

root.reply: docs has the guide and the changelog; site's build output was discarded on purpose. One Sandbox held both Workspaces, and every teardown step was explicit.
